options: The risk that a counterparty fails to meet its obligations
The risk of loss from movements in market prices or rates
The risk of being unable to exit a position without moving its price
The risk that a firm cannot meet its cash obligations as they come due
questions.explain: Market risk is loss from movements in prices or rates such as equities, interest rates, FX, and credit spreads — the risk type VaR and Expected Shortfall were originally built to measure.

questions.q: Which three components multiply together to estimate expected credit loss?
options: Market risk, credit risk, and liquidity risk
Delta, gamma, and vega
Probability of Default (PD), Loss Given Default (LGD), and Exposure at Default (EAD)
VaR, Expected Shortfall, and stress testing
questions.explain: Expected credit loss is estimated as PD times LGD times EAD — the likelihood of default, the fraction of exposure lost if it happens, and the amount owed at that moment.

options: The risk that a position cannot be sold without moving its market price
The risk that a counterparty defaults on a loan
The risk that a firm cannot meet its own cash obligations as they come due, even if solvent on paper
The risk that implied volatility rises unexpectedly
questions.explain: Funding liquidity risk is about a firm's ability to meet its cash obligations in time — a firm can be fundamentally healthy and still fail if it runs out of cash at the wrong moment.

questions.q: A trader needs to unload a large position quickly, and doing so pushes the price down against them. Which risk type does this illustrate?
options: Credit risk
Market liquidity risk
Probability of Default
Funding liquidity risk
questions.explain: Market liquidity risk is the risk that a position cannot be exited (or can only be exited at a worse price) because the market for that asset is thin — the trade itself moves the price.

questions.q: How does concentration risk relate to market, credit, and liquidity risk?
options: It is an unrelated fourth risk type with its own separate measurement tools
It only applies to foreign exchange portfolios
It is a theme that magnifies whichever of the three risk types it sits inside, when exposure piles up in one place
It replaces the need to measure market, credit, or liquidity risk separately
questions.explain: Concentration risk isn't a separate fourth category — exposure concentrated in one sector, counterparty, or funding source makes the underlying market, credit, or liquidity risk worse.
